paragraphs: A personal daily planner that works on phone and PC, synced live.

Learning: when a category (e.g. "Accounting") keeps taking you 1.4× longer than your estimate, new tasks in that category are planned 1.4× longer. It weighs recent tasks more, needs a few samples before it trusts itself fully, and falls back to similar task titles when there's no category.
Stack: Next.js 14 (App Router) · Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Realtime) · Tailwind · ical.js. Installable as a PWA.
features: Tasks — add what you need to do and how long you think it takes.
Sort — drag (or tap) each task into the Eisenhower matrix: urgent/important.

Plan — the planner reads your Google and Outlook calendars and suggests slots for your tasks: most important first, only in free time, with a buffer around every lecture and task. Accept all, accept one by one, skip, or…
Now — start a task, pause for breaks, finish it. Every session is recorded.
Review — planned vs. real time per task, and what the planner has learned about each category. Fix sessions you forgot to pause.
